findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured when present. The generator does not do this. When no SurrogateType is set, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers, which never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] or [DataMember] on T. As a result, a referenced type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] is serialized as a string-keyed map instead of an int-keyed array. A member marked [IgnoreMember] is serialized anyway, so data the author excluded leaks onto the wire.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Req2129GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.HonoursMessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType. It expects the generated formatter to omit IgnoredSecretValue and to use WriteArrayHeader (int keys). On head the contractless path emits a string-key formatter that includes IgnoredSecretValue, so the test fails.

findings.claim: The generated formatter's 'contractless' mode differs from the library's existing contractless behaviour. CreateContractlessMembers keeps only public read-write members (IsPublicReadWrite), so get-only public properties are not serialized at all. Types that have only a parameterized constructor are rejected rather than matched to constructor parameters. ContractlessStandardResolver serializes readable get-only members and matches constructors. Payloads from the generated formatter therefore differ from those of the dynamic contractless resolver for the same T.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a referenced class with `public int Id { get; set; }` and `public string Computed => "x";`. Serialize one instance with MessagePackSerializer and ContractlessStandardResolver.Options, and another with the head-generated [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. Compare the bytes: the generated output lacks the 'Computed' key.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change's reading: contractless by default over public read-write members. An optional public `Type? SurrogateType` property on GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute names a compile-time-only surrogate whose [Key]/[IgnoreMember] members are matched to T by name and type. This is the maintainer-suggested surrogate design, and it needs the MsgPack022 diagnostic plus CreateSurrogateMembers.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: The maintainer's 'simplistic' reading: the attribute has no SurrogateType API, and key control comes from attributes already on T, per issue alternative (1) DataContract/DataMember or existing MessagePack attributes. Minimal edit: remove SurrogateType from the attribute, Constants, GeneratedFormatterRequest, MsgPack022 and CreateSurrogateMembers. In GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect, when T has [MessagePackObject] or [DataContract], build members from [Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataMember(Order/Name)]/[IgnoreDataMember] on T; otherwise fall back to CreateContractlessMembers.
